translations.literal: The emperor abandoned the army and fled first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abandoned his army and fled ahead of the troops.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，入晉陽，憂懼不知所之。

translations.literal: On the guichou day, he entered Jinyang, anxious and fearful, not knowing where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day he entered Jinyang, stricken with fear and at a loss for what to do.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大赦。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 帝謂朝臣曰：「周師甚盛，若何？

translations.literal: The emperor said to the court ministers: "The Zhou army is very strong—what shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers: "The Zhou army is overwhelming—what are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 」群臣咸曰：「天命未改，一得一失，自古皆然。

translations.literal: All the ministers said that Heaven's mandate had not changed and that gaining here and losing there had been the way since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers replied as one that Heaven's mandate had not shifted and that kingdoms had always known both victory and defeat.

sentences.zh: 宜停百賦，安慰朝野，收拾遺兵，背城死戰，以存社稷。

translations.literal: They said one should halt all levies, reassure court and country, gather the scattered troops, and fight to the death with one's back to the city walls to preserve the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: They urged him to suspend every tax, steady court and countryside, rally the broken army, and make a last stand behind the city walls to save the realm.

sentences.zh: 」帝意猶豫，欲向北朔州。

translations.literal: The emperor still hesitated and wished to flee north to Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remained undecided and wanted to flee north to Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 乃留安德王延宗、廣甯王孝珩等守晉陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he left Prince Yanzong of Ande, Prince Xiaogong of Guangning, and others to defend Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then left Prince Yanzong of Ande, Prince Xiaogong of Guangning, and others to hold Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 若晉陽不守，卽欲奔突厥。

translations.literal: If Jinyang could not be held, he then intended to flee to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: If Jinyang fell, he planned to flee to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆曰不可，帝不從其言。

translations.literal: All the ministers said this could not be done, but the emperor would not heed their words.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister protested, but the emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司賀拔伏恩、封輔相、慕容鐘葵等宿衛近臣三十餘人西奔周師。

translations.literal: Opening Ceremony Equaling the Three Dukes Heba Fu'en, Feng Fuxiang, Murong Zhongkui, and more than thirty other palace guards and close attendants fled west to the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Fu'en, Feng Fuxiang, Murong Zhongkui, and more than thirty other palace guards and intimate attendants deserted westward to the Zhou camp.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔募兵，遣安德王廷宗為左，廣甯王孝珩為右。

translations.literal: On the yimao day, an edict ordered recruitment of troops and dispatched Prince Yanzong of Ande to the left and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning to the right.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day, an edict called for levies and placed Prince Yanzong of Ande on the left flank and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning on the right.

sentences.zh: 延宗入見，帝告欲向北朔州。

translations.literal: Yanzong entered to see the emperor, who told him he wished to flee north to Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong came before the emperor, who confided that he meant to flee north to Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 延宗泣諫，不從。

translations.literal: Yanzong wept and remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong pleaded through tears, but the emperor would not be moved.

sentences.zh: 帝密遣王康得與中人齊紹等送皇太后、皇太子於北朔州。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly dispatched Wang Kangde and the eunuch Qi Shao and others to escort the empress dowager and crown prince north to Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent Wang Kangde and the eunuch Qi Shao to convey the empress dowager and crown prince north to Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝幸城南軍，勞將士，其夜欲遁，諸將不從。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day, the emperor visited the army south of the city to encourage the troops; that night he wished to slip away, but the generals would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day the emperor went to the southern camp to rally the troops; that night he tried to flee, but his generals refused.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，大赦，改武平七年為隆化元年。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the seventh year of Wuping was changed to the first year of Longhua.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed from Wuping 7 to Longhua 1.

sentences.zh: 其日，穆提婆降周。

translations.literal: That same day, Mu Tipo surrendered to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Mu Tipo defected to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 詔除安德王延宗為相國，委以備禦，延宗流涕受命。

translations.literal: An edict removed Prince Yanzong of Ande from office and made him grand chancellor, entrusting him with defense; Yanzong accepted through tears.
translations.idiomatic: An edict relieved Prince Yanzong of Ande of his post and made him grand chancellor with full authority over the defense; Yanzong accepted the charge in tears.

sentences.zh: 帝乃夜斬五龍門而出，欲走突厥，從官多散。

translations.literal: The emperor then cut through the Wulong Gate by night and went out, intending to flee to the Turks; many of his attendants scattered.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor cut through the Wulong Gate intending to flee to the Turks, and most of his attendants scattered.

sentences.zh: 領軍梅勝郎叩馬諫，乃廻之鄴。

translations.literal: Leading Army Commander Mei Sheng seized the bridle and remonstrated, whereupon he turned back toward Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Leading Army Commander Mei Sheng seized his horse's bridle and pleaded with him, and the emperor turned back toward Ye.

sentences.zh: 時唯高阿那肱等十餘騎，廣甯王孝珩、襄城王彥道續至，得數十人同行。

translations.literal: At that time only Gao Anaggon and a dozen or so horsemen remained; Prince Xiaogong of Guangning and Prince Yandao of Xiangcheng caught up afterward, and they had several dozen men traveling together.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gao Anaggon and a dozen riders were still with him; Prince Xiaogong of Guangning and Prince Yandao of Xiangcheng soon joined them, bringing their party to several dozen men.

sentences.zh: 戊午，延宗從衆議卽皇帝位於晉陽，改隆化為德昌元年。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day, Yanzong, yielding to the will of the assembly, immediately took the throne at Jinyang and changed Longhua to the first year of Dechang.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day Yanzong, bowing to the will of the assembly, immediately ascended the throne at Jinyang and changed the era name to Dechang 1.

sentences.zh: 庚申，帝入鄴。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day, the emperor entered Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day the emperor entered Ye.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，延宗與周師戰於晉陽，大敗，為周師所虜。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day, Yanzong fought the Zhou army at Jinyang, was routed, and was captured by the Zhou forces.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day Yanzong fought the Zhou army at Jinyang, was defeated, and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 帝遣募人，重加官賞，雖有此言，而竟不出物。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered recruitment of men with heavy rewards of office and bounty; though he spoke thus, in the end he furnished nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called for recruits with lavish promises of rank and reward, but in the end provided nothing.

sentences.zh: 廣甯王孝珩奏請出宮人及珍寶班賜將士，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Prince Xiaogong of Guangning memorialized asking that palace women and treasures be distributed to the troops, and the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaogong of Guangning petitioned to distribute palace women and treasures among the troops, and the emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 斛律孝卿居中受委，帶甲以處分，請帝親勞，為帝撰辭，且曰宜慷慨流涕，感激人心。

translations.literal: Hulu Xiaoqing, holding delegated authority at court, wore armor to direct affairs; he asked the emperor to address the troops in person, drafted a speech for him, and said he ought to speak with generous tears to stir the hearts of the men.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Xiaoqing, wielding delegated authority at court, appeared in armor to direct affairs; he urged the emperor to address the troops in person, drafted a speech for him, and said he should speak through generous tears to stir their hearts.

sentences.zh: 帝旣出臨衆，將令之，不復記所受言，遂大笑，左右亦群咍，將士莫不解體。

translations.literal: When the emperor came out before the assembly and was about to address them, he no longer remembered what he had been told to say; he burst into loud laughter instead, and those around him all guffawed with him, so that the soldiers entirely lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor appeared before the troops and tried to speak, he forgot every word he had been given and burst out laughing; his attendants joined in, and the soldiers' morale collapsed entirely.

sentences.zh: 於是自大丞相已下太宰、三師、大司馬、大將軍、三公等官並增員而授，或三或四，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Thereupon from grand chancellor downward, grand tutor, the three preceptors, grand marshal, grand general, and the three dukes and other offices all had their quotas increased and appointments made, some to three or four men each, beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon posts from grand chancellor down through grand tutor, the three preceptors, grand marshal, grand general, and the three dukes were multiplied, some offices filled three or four at a time, beyond number.

sentences.zh: 甲子，皇太后從北道至。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day, the empress dowager arrived by the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day the empress dowager arrived by the northern road.

sentences.zh: 引文武一品已上入朱華門，賜酒食，給紙筆，問以禦周之方。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of the first rank and above were summoned into the Zhuhua Gate, given wine and food, provided paper and brush, and asked for plans to resist Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned civil and military officials of the first rank and above to the Zhuhua Gate, feasted them, supplied paper and brush, and asked how Zhou might be resisted.

sentences.zh: 群臣各異議，帝莫知所從。

translations.literal: The ministers each offered different proposals, and the emperor did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Each minister offered a different plan, and the emperor could not decide whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 又引高元海、宋士素、盧思道、李德林等，欲議禪位皇太子。

translations.literal: He then summoned Gao Yuanhai, Song Shisu, Lu Sidao, Li Delin, and others, intending to deliberate on abdicating the throne to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Gao Yuanhai, Song Shisu, Lu Sidao, Li Delin, and others to discuss abdicating in favor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 先是望氣者言，當有革易，終是依天統故事，授位幼主。

translations.literal: Earlier, diviners of celestial signs had said there would be a dynastic change; in the end they followed the precedent of the Tian Tong era and transferred the throne to Youzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier court diviners had foretold a change of dynasty; in the end the court followed the Tian Tong precedent and transferred the throne to Youzhu.

sentences.zh: 幼主名恒，帝之長子也。

translations.literal: Youzhu, personal name Heng, was the emperor's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhu, whose personal name was Heng, was the emperor's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 母曰穆皇后，武平元年六月生於鄴。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Mu; he was born at Ye in the sixth month of the first year of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Mu; he was born at Ye in the sixth month of the first year of the Wuping era.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he was formally established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 隆化二年春正月乙亥，卽皇帝位，時八歲，改元為承光元年，大赦，尊皇太后為太皇太后，帝為太上皇帝，後為太上皇后。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the second year of Longhua, on the yihai day, he immediately took the throne; he was eight years old; the era name was changed to Chengguang 1; a general amnesty was proclaimed; the empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager; the emperor became retired emperor; and the empress became retired empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of Longhua 2, on the yihai day, he immediately ascended the throne at the age of eight; the era was renamed Chengguang 1; a general amnesty was proclaimed; the empress dowager was elevated to grand empress dowager; the former emperor became retired emperor; and the empress became retired empress.

sentences.zh: 於是黃門侍郎顏之推、中書侍郎薛道衡、侍中陳德信等勸太上皇帝往河外募兵，更為經略，若不濟，南投陳國，從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yellow Gate Gentleman Yan Zhitui, Masters of Writing Gentleman Xue Daohang, Palace Attendant Chen Dexin, and others urged the retired emperor to go beyond the Yellow River to recruit troops and renew strategic planning; if that failed, they should flee south and submit to Chen—and he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Gentleman Yan Zhitui, Masters of Writing Gentleman Xue Daohang, Palace Attendant Chen Dexin, and others then urged the retired emperor to cross the Yellow River to raise troops and regroup; if that failed, they should flee south to Chen—and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，太皇太后、太上皇后自鄴先趣濟州。

translations.literal: On the dingchou day, the grand empress dowager and retired empress left Ye first and hastened to Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day the grand empress dowager and retired empress departed Ye ahead of the court and hurried toward Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 周師漸逼，癸未，幼主又自鄴東走。

translations.literal: As the Zhou army pressed closer, on the guimao day Youzhu again fled east from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou forces closed in, on the guimao day Youzhu fled east from Ye once more.

sentences.zh: 己丑，周師至紫陌橋。

translations.literal: On the jichou day, the Zhou army reached Zimo Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day the Zhou army reached Zimo Bridge.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，燒城西門。

translations.literal: On the guisi day, the western gate of the city was burned.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day the western gate of the city was set ablaze.

sentences.zh: 太上皇將百餘騎東走。

translations.literal: The retired emperor fled east with a little more than a hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor fled east with barely a hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，渡河入濟州。

translations.literal: On the yihai day, he crossed the river and entered Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day he crossed the river and entered Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 其日，幼主禪位於大丞相、任城王湝，令侍中斛律孝卿送禪文及璽紱於瀛州，孝卿乃以之歸周。

translations.literal: That same day Youzhu abdicated the throne to Grand Chancellor Prince Ji of Rencheng and ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaoqing to deliver the abdication document and imperial seal and cord to Ying Province; Xiaoqing instead took them to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Youzhu abdicated in favor of Grand Chancellor Prince Ji of Rencheng and ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaoqing to convey the abdication text and imperial seal and cord to Ying Province—but Xiaoqing delivered them to Zhou instead.

sentences.zh: 又為任城王詔，尊太上皇為無上皇，幼主為守國天王。

translations.literal: Prince Ji also issued an edict in his own name honoring the retired emperor as supreme retired emperor and Youzhu as guardian king of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji also issued an edict in his own name, elevating the retired emperor to supreme retired emperor and naming Youzhu guardian king of the realm.

sentences.zh: 留太皇太后濟州，遣高阿那肱留守。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager was left at Ji Province, and Gao Anaggon was dispatched to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager was left at Ji Province with Gao Anaggon assigned to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 太上皇並皇后攜幼主走青州，韓長鸞、鄧顒等數十人從。

translations.literal: The retired emperor, the empress, and Youzhu fled to Qing Province, accompanied by Han Changluan, Deng Yan, and several dozen others.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor, the empress, and Youzhu fled toward Qing Province with Han Changluan, Deng Yan, and several dozen followers.

sentences.zh: 太上皇旣至青州，卽為入陳之計。

translations.literal: Once the retired emperor reached Qing Province, he immediately planned entry into Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Once the retired emperor reached Qing Province, he immediately set about planning flight into Chen.

sentences.zh: 而高阿那肱召周軍，約生致齊主，而屢使人告言，賊軍在遠，已令人燒斷橋路。

translations.literal: But Gao Anaggon summoned the Zhou army, agreeing to deliver the Qi ruler alive, yet repeatedly sent word saying the enemy was still far off and that he had already had the bridges and roads burned.
translations.idiomatic: But Gao Anaggon had summoned the Zhou army, promising to deliver the Qi ruler alive, while repeatedly reporting that the enemy was still distant and that he had already burned the bridges and roads.

sentences.zh: 太上所以停緩。

translations.literal: For this reason the retired emperor halted and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the retired emperor paused and delayed his flight.

sentences.zh: 周軍奄至青州，太上窘急，將遜於陳，置金囊於鞍後，與長鸞、淑妃等十數騎至青州南鄧村，為周將尉遲綱所獲。

translations.literal: The Zhou army suddenly reached Qing Province; the retired emperor, in desperate straits and about to withdraw into Chen, placed a gold pouch behind his saddle; with Changluan, the consort, and a dozen or so riders he reached Deng Village south of Qing Province and was captured by the Zhou general Yuchi Gang.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army suddenly appeared at Qing Province; cornered and about to slip into Chen, the retired emperor hung a gold pouch from his saddle and rode south with Changluan, his consort, and a dozen followers to Deng Village south of the city, where Zhou general Yuchi Gang seized them.

sentences.zh: 送鄴，周武帝與抗賓主禮，並太后、幼主、諸王俱送長安，封帝溫國公。

translations.literal: They were sent to Ye; Emperor Wu of Zhou received the retired emperor with the courtesies due a guest of equal rank; the empress dowager, Youzhu, and the princes were all sent to Chang'an, and the retired emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: They were sent to Ye, where Emperor Wu of Zhou received the retired emperor with the courtesies due an equal; the empress dowager, Youzhu, and the princes were all sent to Chang'an, and the retired emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen.

sentences.zh: 至建德七年，誣與宜州刺史穆提婆謀反，及延宗等數十人無少長咸賜死，神武子孫所存者一二而已。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiande he was falsely accused of plotting rebellion with Governor of Yizhou Mu Tipo; Yanzong and several dozen others, without distinction of age, were all granted death; of Shenwu's descendants only one or two remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jiande era he was falsely accused of plotting rebellion with Mu Tipo, governor of Yizhou; Yanzong and dozens of others, young and old alike, were put to death; of Shenwu's descendants only one or two survived.

sentences.zh: 至大象末，陽休之、陳德信等啟大丞相隋公，請收葬，聽之，葬長安北原洪瀆川。

translations.literal: By the end of the Daxiang era, Yang Xiuzhi, Chen Dexin, and others petitioned Grand Chancellor Duke Sui, asking permission to gather the remains for burial; permission was granted, and they were buried at Hongdu Stream on the northern plain of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daxiang era Yang Xiuzhi, Chen Dexin, and others petitioned Grand Chancellor the Duke of Sui for permission to bury the remains; he consented, and they were interred at Hongdu Stream on the northern plain of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝幼而令善，及長，頗學綴文，置文林館，引諸文士焉。

translations.literal: The emperor was good and well behaved from childhood; when grown he studied composition to some degree, established the Forest of Letters Hall, and gathered literary men there.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy the emperor was well behaved; as he grew he took up literary composition, established the Forest of Letters Hall, and gathered scholars there.

sentences.zh: 而言語澀呐，無志度，不喜見朝士。

translations.literal: Yet his speech was halting, he lacked resolution, and he disliked meeting court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he spoke haltingly, lacked firm purpose, and disliked receiving court officials.

sentences.zh: 自非寵私昵狎，未嘗交語，性懦不堪，人視者，卽有忿責。

translations.literal: Unless they were favorites or intimate companions, he never exchanged words with them; he was timid and could not bear to be looked at—whoever gazed at him he at once rebuked in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Unless they were favorites or intimate companions he never spoke with them; craven and unable to endure being watched, he would fly into a rage at anyone who looked at him.

sentences.zh: 其奏事者，雖三公令錄莫得仰視，皆略陳大旨，驚走而出。

translations.literal: Those who submitted memorials—even the three dukes and chief ministers—might not raise their eyes to look at him; they could only sketch the main points, then flee out in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Even the three dukes and chief ministers reporting to him dared not meet his gaze; they could only outline the gist of their business and flee in alarm.

sentences.zh: 每災異寇盜水旱，亦不貶損，唯諸處設齋，以此為修德。

translations.literal: Whenever there were calamities, banditry, or flood and drought, he never reduced expenditures or humbled himself; he only ordered vegetarian feasts at various places, taking that as cultivation of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever disaster, banditry, flood, or drought struck, he never cut spending or humbled himself; he merely ordered vegetarian offerings here and there, calling that moral cultivation.

sentences.zh: 雅信巫覡，解禱無方。

translations.literal: He trusted shamans implicitly and knew no method of prayer or expiation beyond them.
translations.idiomatic: He put blind faith in shamans and knew no remedy for prayer or expiation beyond them.

sentences.zh: 初琅邪王舉兵，人告者誤云厙狄伏連反，帝曰：「此必仁威也。

translations.literal: At first when the Prince of Langye raised troops, the informant wrongly said Kudivolian had rebelled, and the emperor said this must be Renwei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Langye first rose in arms, an informant wrongly reported that Kudivolian had rebelled, and the emperor said this must be Renwei.

sentences.zh: 」又斛律光死後，諸武官舉高思好堪大將軍，帝曰：「思好喜反。

translations.literal: Later, after Hulu Guang died, the military officers recommended Gao Sihao as fit for grand general, and the emperor said Sihao was fond of rebelling.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Hulu Guang's death, the military officers recommended Gao Sihao for grand general, and the emperor said Sihao was always ready to rebel.

sentences.zh: 」皆如所言。

translations.literal: On every occasion it proved exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: On every occasion events proved exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 遂自以策無遺算，乃益驕縱。
盛為無愁之曲，帝自彈胡琵琶而唱之，侍和之者以百數。
人間謂之無愁天子。
嘗出見羣厲，盡殺之，或剝人面皮而視之。
任陸令萱、和士開、高阿那肱、穆提婆、韓長鸞等宰製天下，陳德信、鄧長顒、何洪珍參預機權。
各引親党，超居非次，官由財進，獄以賄成，其所以亂政害人，難以備載。
諸宮奴婢、閹人、商人、胡戶、雜戶、歌舞人、見鬼人濫得富貴者將萬數，庶姓封王者百數，不復可紀。
開府千餘，儀同無數。
領軍一時二十，連判文書，各作依字，不具姓名，莫知誰也。
諸貴寵祖禰追贈官，歲一進，位極乃止。
宮掖婢皆封郡君，宮女寶衣玉食者五百餘人，一裙直萬疋，鏡臺直千金，競為變巧，朝衣夕弊。
承武成之奢麗，以為帝王當然。
乃更增益宮苑，造偃武修文臺，其嬪嬙諸宮中起鏡殿、寶殿、瑇瑁殿，丹青雕刻，妙極當時。
又於晉陽起十二院，壯麗逾於鄴下。
所愛不恒，數毀而又復。
夜則以火照作，寒則以湯為泥，百工困窮，無時休息。
鑿晉陽西山為大佛像，一夜然油萬盆，光照宮內。
又為胡昭儀起大慈寺，未成，改為穆皇后大寶林寺，窮極工巧，運石填泉，勞費億計，人牛死者不可勝紀。
御馬則藉以氊罽，食物有十餘種，將合牝牡，則設青廬，具牢饌而親觀之。
狗則飼以粱肉。
馬及鷹犬乃有儀同、郡君之號，故有赤彪儀同、逍遙郡君、淩霄郡君，高思好書所謂「駮龍、逍遙」者也。
犬於馬上設褥以抱之，鬬雞亦號開府，犬馬雞鷹多食縣幹。
鷹之入養者，稍割犬肉以飼之，至數日乃死。
又於華林園立貧窮村舍，帝自弊衣為乞食兒。
又為窮兒之市，躬自交易。
嘗築西鄙諸城，使人衣黑衣為羌兵，鼓噪淩之，親率內參臨拒，或實彎弓射人。
自晉陽東巡，單馬馳騖，衣解髮散而歸。
又好不急之務，曾一夜索蠍，及旦得三升。
特愛非時之物，取求火急，皆須朝徵夕辦，當勢者因之，貸一而責十焉。
賦斂日重，徭役日繁，人力旣殫，幣藏空竭。
乃賜諸佞幸賣官。
或得郡兩三，或得縣六七，各分州郡，下逮鄉官亦多降中旨，故有勑用州主簿，勑用郡功曹。
於是州縣職司多出富商大賈，競為貪縱，人不聊生。
爰自鄴都及諸州郡，所在徵稅，百端俱起。
凡此諸役，皆漸於武成，至帝而增廣焉。
然未嘗有帷薄淫穢，唯此事頗優於武成云。
初河清末，武成夢大蝟攻破鄴城，故索境內蝟膏以絕之。
識者以後主名聲與蝟相協，亡齊徵也。
又婦人皆剪剔以著假髻，而危邪之狀如飛鳥，至於南面，則髻心正西。
始自宮內為之，被於四遠，天意若曰元首剪落，危側當走西也。
又為刀子者刃皆狹細，名曰盡勢。
游童戲者好以兩手持繩，拂地而卻上跳，且唱曰「高末」，高未之言，蓋高氏運祚之末也。
然則亂亡之數蓋有兆云。
論曰：武成風度高爽，經算弘長，文武之官，俱盡其力，有帝王之量矣。
但愛狎庸豎，委以朝權，帷薄之間，淫侈過度，滅亡之兆，其在斯乎？
玄象告變，傳位元子，名號雖殊，政猶己出，跡有虛飾，事非憲典，聰明臨下，何易可誣。
又河南、河間、樂陵等諸王，或以時嫌，或以猜忌，皆無罪而殞，非所謂知命任天道之義也。
後主以中庸之姿，懷易染之性，永言先訓，教匪義方。
始自繈褓，至于傳位，隔以正人，閉其善道。
養德所履，異乎春誦夏弦；
過庭所聞，莫非不軌不物。
輔之以中宮嬭媼，屬之以麗色淫聲，縱韝絏之娛，恣朋淫之好。
語曰「從惡若崩」，蓋言其易。
武平在御，彌見淪胥，罕接朝士，不親政事，一日萬機，委諸凶族。
內侍帷幄，外吐絲綸，威厲風霜，志廻天日，虐人害物，搏噬無厭，賣獄鬻官，溪壑難滿。
重以名將貽禍，忠臣顯戮，始見浸弱之萌，俄觀土崩之勢，周武因機，遂混區夏，悲夫！
蓋桀、紂罪人，其亡也忽焉，自然之理矣。
鄭文貞公魏徵總而論之曰：神武以雄傑之姿，始基霸業；
文襄以英明之略，伐叛柔遠。
于時喪君有君，師出以律。
河陰之役，摧宇文如反掌；
渦陽之戰，掃侯景如拉枯。
故能氣攝西鄰，威加南服，王室是賴，東夏宅心。
文宣因累世之資，膺樂推之會，地居當璧，遂遷魏鼎。
懷譎詭非常之才，運屈奇不測之智，網羅俊乂，明察臨下，文武名臣，盡其力用。
親戎出塞，命將臨江，定單于於龍城，納長君於梁國，外內充實，疆埸無警，胡騎息其南侵，秦人不敢東顧。
旣而荒淫敗德，罔念作狂，為善未能亡身，餘殃足以傳後。
得以壽終，幸也，胤嗣不永，宜哉。
孝昭地逼身危，逆取順守，外敷文教，內蘊雄圖，將以牢籠區域，奄一函夏，享齡不永，勣用無成。
若或天假之年，足使秦、吳旰食。
武成卽位，雅道陵遲，昭、襄之風，漼焉已墜。
洎乎後主，外內崩離，衆潰於平陽，身離於青土。
天道深遠，或未易談，吉凶由人，抑可揚榷。
觀夫有齊全盛，控帶遐阻，西苞汾、晉，南極江、淮，東盡海隅，北漸沙漠，六國之地，我獲其五，九州之境，彼分其四。
料甲兵之衆寡，校帑藏之虛實，折衝千里之將，帷幄六奇之士，比二方之優劣，無等級以寄言。
然其太行、長城之固自若也，江淮、汾晉之險不移也，帑藏輸稅之賦未虧也，士庶甲兵之衆不缺也；
然而前王用之而有餘，後主守之而不足，其故何哉？
前王之御時也，沐雨櫛風，拯其溺而救其焚，信賞必罰，安而利之，旣與共其存亡，故得同其生死。
後主則不然，以人從欲，損物益己。
雕牆峻宇，甘酒嗜音，廛肆遍於宮園，禽色荒於外內，俾晝作夜，罔水行舟，所欲必成，所求必得。
旣不軌不物，又暗於聽受，忠信不聞，萋斐必入，視人如草芥，從惡如順流。
佞閹處當軸之權，婢媼擅廻天之力，賣官鬻獄，亂政淫刑，刳剒被於忠良，祿位加於犬馬，讒邪並進，法令多聞，持瓢者非止百人，搖樹者不唯一手，於是土崩瓦解，衆叛親離，顧瞻周道，咸有西歸之志，方更盛其宮觀，窮極荒淫，謂黔首之可誣，指白日以自保。
馳倒戈之旅，抗前歌之師，五世崇基，一舉而滅，豈非鐫金石者難為功，摧枯朽者易為力歟？
抑又聞之：皇天無親，唯德是輔；
天時不如地利，地利不如人和。
齊自河清之後，逮于武平之末，土木之功不息，嬪嬙之選無已，征稅盡，人力殫，物產無以給其求，江海不能贍其欲。
所謂火旣熾矣，更負薪以足之，數旣窮矣，又為惡以促之，欲求大廈不燔，延期過曆，不亦難乎！
由此言之，齊氏之敗亡，蓋亦由人，匪唯天道也。
